title: go-sdk: graceful stream closure and timeout integration for ReadStream API
creator: Avery Cole
description:
Goal: Implement a robust streaming implementation in the Go SDK for the ReadStream/ChatStream APIs that properly integrates context cancellation, per-request timeouts, and user-visible backpressure semantics. The work should avoid surprising goroutine leaks, ensure prompt stream closure on context cancellation or deadline expiry, and provide clear retry/rewind semantics for transient network errors.

Design constraints and non-goals:
- This ticket focuses on SDK-side behavior only (runtime/server changes are out of scope).
- We should not change the wire protocol or server-side session semantics.
- Keep the public API ergonomic for common usage patterns: simple streaming use, streaming with explicit per-message timeouts, and streaming with an overall request deadline.

Proposed API surface (informal):
- type StreamReader interface {
    Recv(ctx context.Context) (Message, error) // respects ctx cancellation and deadline
    Close() error // idempotent graceful close, signals server to free resources when possible
    CloseWithError(err error) error // optionally send final error/annotation to server logs
  }
- NewStream(ctx, reqOpts...) (StreamReader, error) // accepts WithDeadline/WithTimeout helpers

Key behaviors to implement:
1) Context propagation: every Recv call must accept a caller ctx; if ctx.Done() fires, Recv returns promptly with ctx.Err() and ensures any internal goroutines are stopped.
2) Per-call and total request timeouts: support both per-message timeout wrappers and an overall request deadline that cancels the underlying network stream.
3) Backpressure and buffering: keep a small, configurable internal read buffer (default 1-2 messages) to smooth bursts but not to hide network slowdowns; document buffer behavior.
4) Retry semantics: for transient network failures during streaming, provide a deterministic behavior: either surface an error immediately (default) or opt into automatic reconnect-with-offset for idempotent streams. Provide helper utilities for common patterns.
5) Leak prevention: ensure any goroutine started by NewStream returns on Close/ctx cancel, even in the face of slow servers or network partitions.
6) Examples: include at least two examples in repository: a simple streaming consumer with context.WithTimeout, and a resilient consumer using reconnect helpers and message checkpointing.
acceptance_criteria: Go SDK exposes a StreamReader with Recv(ctx) that returns promptly on ctx cancellation
Unit tests demonstrating Recv returns ctx.Err() when a caller context is cancelled
Stress test showing no goroutine growth after repeated open/close/cancel cycles
Documentation examples for simple timeout and resilient reconnect patterns
A design doc reviewed by SDK and Runtime teams and a PR merged to main
Benchmarks for default buffer sizes and one alternative buffer size included in CI
